failure_modes.what: The ramp board and every order-sync callback (skipRamp not set) creates RAMP rows via POST on page open/day-change/order-save, with no user click and no owner decision on record authorizing 'the ramp auto-creates on open'.
failure_modes.gap: A dispatcher who opens the board never learns that visiting the page just wrote data; only a partial failure produces a toast (and only for the actor who happened to be looking).

failure_modes.what: Marking a ramp row 'Done' only promotes the parent order to In Transit when the row carries an Order/National Order/National Load link. Historical rows created before the links block existed (0/44 measured 6/9/2026) have no link.
failure_modes.gap: Clicking Done on an unlinked historical row does nothing to the order and shows no message explaining why -- looks identical to success.

failure_modes.what: Reads r.fields['Client Name'], a label that does not exist anywhere in the ORDERS worker map (only a 'Client' link to clients.id exists). It is always undefined, so every order's client name falls back to the literal string 'Unknown'.
failure_modes.gap: The CEO Dashboard's Top Clients KPI silently renders 100% of period revenue under a single 'Unknown' bucket -- looks like real, if odd, data, no error, no ESTIMATE badge (unlike the sibling _calcDeadKM function 40 lines below it, which does guard this exact class of problem correctly).

failure_modes.what: core/metrics.js#captureMetricSnapshot(Batch) writes to TABLES.METRICS_SNAPSHOTS (facade id tblakFiR37kf4uQXy from config.js:80), but that id has NO entry anywhere in the worker's TABLES map -- a call would get 'Table not available on this backend' (404). No module calls these functions today.
failure_modes.gap: Dead on both ends right now; the risk is someone wiring a caller to it later, testing manually, getting a 404, and not realizing the whole path needs a Worker-side table entry too.

failure_modes.what: /api/locations (GET+POST) is a fully RBAC-gated, working endpoint with its own narrower write allowlist (LOCATION_FIELDS = legacy_id/name/address/city/country only), but no frontend file calls it -- modules/locations.js always uses the generic /v0/<tableId> facade instead.
failure_modes.gap: Nobody would notice this endpoint drifting from the facade's LOCATIONS field map (it already has: it's missing type/lat/lon/opening_hours/delivery_days/notes/phone/tags) because nothing exercises it in production.

failure_modes.what: config.js defines SCAN_TRAINING twice in the same TABLES object literal: line 79 sets it to the correct facade id 'tblScanTraining000' (which matches a real, fully-wired worker table at worker/src/index.js:1742-1746), then line 85 immediately overwrites it with ''. JS object literals keep only the last duplicate key, so TABLES.SCAN_TRAINING is always '' at runtime.
failure_modes.gap: core/scan-helpers.js:352-360 correctly guards `if (tableId && ...)` before writing, so this never throws -- it just quietly never shares scan corrections across users/devices, forever, and the stale comment above line 85 ('SCAN_TRAINING: optional... paste its table id below') reads as if the feature was never built, when in fact the Worker side has been ready since the scan_examples schema landed (comment cites 10/8).

failure_modes.what: The AI's update_record tool passes whatever `fields` object the model produced straight into atPatch(TABLES[tKey], record_id, fields) with no client-side field-name validation.
failure_modes.gap: If the model sends a field label the Worker map does not recognize for that table (typo, hallucinated English label, wrong casing), buildWriteRow drops it (worker/src/index.js:2340-2344) and the PATCH still returns 200 -- ai-chat.js shows toast('Record updated','success') regardless (core/ai-chat.js:578). The Phase-1 unknown-field logger (facade_unknown_fields) does catch this server-side, but nobody is watching that table in real time.

failure_modes.what: The Worker exposes a safe, authenticated, server-key-holding proxy at POST /v1/ai/messages, but core/ai-chat.js calls https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages directly from the browser instead, using a client-side ANTH_KEY constant that is '' in this repo's config.js:46.
failure_modes.visibility: loud (if ANTH_KEY stays empty: every AI chat call fails with 401) / silent (as a design drift: the safer server path sits unused)
failure_modes.gap: Two competing implementations of the same call exist; only one is exercised by the app, and it is the one that would expose a real key to the browser if ANTH_KEY were ever populated. Out of scope for this pass to assess further (security), flagged per 02a F-40's own note.
